# Oracle: Consolidated Agent Context

> Oracle is a persistent context, guarded action, and durable coordination layer for AI coding agents.

## Purpose

Oracle is not a generic chat shell. It assembles selected workspace context,
injects an explicit operating identity and boundary, routes work to a
configured execution backend, and records the result. Its autonomous agent,
messaging, task, Runtime, Control Center, and Remote Swarm surfaces extend the
same model into guarded action and durable coordination.

Repository: https://github.com/OraclePersonal/Oracle
Package: @jonusnattapong/oracle
License: MIT
Runtime requirement: Node.js >= 24

## First Run

```bash
npm install -g @jonusnattapong/oracle
codex login
oracle doctor
oracle ask "Map the error-handling path and identify one missing test" -f "src/**/*.ts"
```

The default execution backend is the locally authenticated Codex CLI.

To connect Oracle to an MCP host:

```bash
oracle setup-mcp --client codex
oracle setup-mcp --client claude-code
```

## Interfaces

- `oracle`: human- and script-facing CLI.
- `oracle-mcp`: full stdio MCP server.
- `oracle-msg-mcp`: coordination-only stdio MCP server.
- `oracle-daemon`: persistent Runtime service.

The full MCP server exposes consultation, agent, memory, docs, web, identity,
session, diagnostics, messaging, task, coordination, history, and GitHub
tools. Connected clients receive instructions for agent registration,
inbox handling, and verified task flow.

## Core Capabilities

### Awareness

Oracle derives its live operating context from:

- Oracle persona and functional role;
- configured operator identity;
- current interface (`cli`, `mcp`, `runtime`, or `agent`);
- workspace label;
- selected execution backend;
- read-only state when relevant;
- capabilities available on that interface;
- explicit operating boundaries.

Prompt-bound awareness uses the workspace label instead of sending the
absolute local workspace path to an external backend.

### Consultation

`oracle ask` and `oracle_ask`:

- accept a question plus selected paths or globs;
- resolve files inside the active workspace;
- apply file-size and aggregate-input limits;
- detect likely secrets before outbound transmission;
- optionally retrieve project memory and `.oracle/docs/`;
- route through a configured backend;
- store sessions under `~/.oracle/sessions/<id>/`;
- support logical conversation continuation when the backend can resume.

### Memory and Local Knowledge

Oracle supports project/global facts, insights, chunks, working entries,
ranked retrieval, local docs search, entity relationships, optional embedding
providers, maintenance, and topic wiki compilation. Provider-dependent
features must be configured before use.

### Autonomous Agent

`oracle agent` and `oracle_agent` run a multi-turn tool loop with workspace
file tools and policy-checked command execution. Agent commands and Runtime
schedules share an execution runner that records each result in Runtime SQLite.

Controls include:

- read-only mode that removes mutating tools;
- maximum turn ceilings;
- workspace path confinement;
- policy and risk assessment;
- human approval modes (`off`, `risky`, `all-mutations`);
- checkpoints and resume;
- audit evidence;
- optional plan-first and self-review flows.

The default command boundary is policy-constrained, not a kernel sandbox.
Set `.oracle/policy.json` `sandbox.mode` to `docker` for fail-closed Docker
execution: only the workspace is mounted, root is read-only, network defaults
to denied, and environment variables require an allow-list. Inspect the active
state with `oracle sandbox doctor`; see `docs/sandbox.md` for limitations.

### Coordination

Local coordination uses a shared SQLite store and includes:

- named agent presence;
- direct and broadcast messages;
- inbox wait and acknowledgement;
- durable task assignment;
- checklist-gated submission;
- creator review and rejection;
- consensus proposals and votes;
- recovery of interrupted task-to-message delivery.

Task submission is blocked while any required checklist item remains
unchecked.

### Runtime and Control

The Runtime owns:

- SQLite state at `~/.oracle/runtime/oracle.db`;
- long-lived schedules and run history;
- authenticated loopback HTTP APIs;
- replayable WebSocket events;
- approval requests, votes, expiry, and execution claims;
- Control Center data;
- Remote Swarm endpoints.

Default endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:4777`.

```bash
oracle daemon start
oracle daemon status
oracle control
```

### Remote Swarm

Remote Swarm provides project-scoped presence, messages, tasks, and event
replay across machines. It is a coordination plane, not a remote execution
plane.

Remote tokens do not grant:

- shell or filesystem access;
- Scheduler access;
- approval authority;
- Runtime administration.

Raw agent tokens are printed once. Oracle stores SHA-256 token hashes. The
built-in server is HTTP; non-loopback deployments require TLS termination or
an encrypted private network.

## Execution Backends

- `codex`: consultation and agent loop; uses local Codex CLI login.
- `anthropic`: consultation and agent loop; API key or Oracle OAuth login.
- `openai`: consultation; OpenAI API credentials.
- `gemini`: consultation; Gemini/Google API credentials.
- `opencode`: consultation and agent loop; OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- `azure`: consultation; Azure OpenAI configuration.
- `openrouter`: consultation; OpenRouter configuration.
- `chatgpt-browser`: experimental consultation through a visible, isolated
  Chrome profile and manual ChatGPT login.

Browser Mode is local-interactive UI automation, not the OpenAI API. It does
not support the autonomous agent loop and should not be presented as an
unattended production backend.

## Project State

Project-local state:

```text
<workspace>/.oracle/
  config.json
  policy.json
  docs/
  skills/
  audit.jsonl
```

User-level state:

```text
~/.oracle/
  runtime/oracle.db
  sessions/
  memory/
  souls/
  oracles/
  remote.json
```

## Trust Boundaries

1. Workspace paths must remain inside the active project boundary.
2. Outbound selected context is size-limited and secret-scanned.
3. Agent mutation is a separate, policy-controlled capability.
4. Docker sandbox mode adds isolated execution and never silently falls back to host execution.
5. Runtime admin tokens and Remote Swarm project tokens are distinct.
6. Remote Swarm does not expose execution powers.
7. Browser Mode uses an isolated visible profile and remains experimental.
8. ACTB governance status describes built-in controls; it is not a compliance
   or security certification.

## Command Map

```text
oracle ask                  grounded consultation
oracle agent                autonomous or read-only coding loop
oracle memory / wiki        memory inspection and compilation
oracle docs / web           local knowledge and configured retrieval
oracle msg / task           local coordination and verification
oracle team / swarm         remote and consensus workflows
oracle daemon / schedule    persistent Runtime and cron ownership
oracle control / approval   human oversight
oracle identity             operator, persona, and awareness
oracle audit / governance   evidence and policy status
oracle sandbox doctor       execution boundary and Docker readiness
oracle github               pull requests and issues through gh
oracle browser              experimental ChatGPT Browser Mode
```

## Development and Verification

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm test
npm run test:cli
npm run test:runtime
```

The release gate is:

```bash
npm run verify
```
